//==
// # IGeometry
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - IGeometry classification and topological markers
//  - IFitted-shape interface
//  - IGeometry bounds, point sets, measures, and centroids
//  - IGeometry point queries

//==
// # IGeometry classification and topological markers
//
// What a geometric entity IS: the root marker, the embedding-dimension family
// (IGeometry2D / IGeometry3D / IGeometryND), and the pure structural markers a shape
// promises (open, closed, convex, manifold, orientable, connected). Intrinsic
// (topological) dimension is NOT a member here: it is already implied by which
// family a type belongs to (ICurve*, ISurface, ISolid). The `Dimensioned` interface
// was retired unimplemented. The capability interfaces that say what can be QUERIED on
// such an entity follow in the sections below.

//==
// # Classification

// The root marker for every geometric entity: an immutable value describing a
// locus of points in some space. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(mathematics))
interface IGeometry
    inherits IValue
{ }

// IGeometry embedded in the 2D Cartesian plane.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_plane)
interface IGeometry2D
    inherits IGeometry
{ }

// IGeometry embedded in 3D Cartesian space.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-dimensional_space)
interface IGeometry3D
    inherits IGeometry
{ }

// IGeometry embedded in an N-dimensional space whose dimension is known only at
// runtime.
interface IGeometryND
    inherits IGeometry
{ }

//==
// # Topological markers
//
// Pure markers: they declare structural facts a shape promises, and carry no
// functions of their own.

// Marks a shape whose boundary has free ends and does not close on itself:
// an arc, an open polyline, a curve span.
interface IOpenShape
{ }

// Marks a shape that closes on itself and separates inside from outside:
// a circle, a polygon, a sphere, a solid.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_curve_theorem)
interface IClosedShape
{ }

// Marks a shape that contains the entire straight segment between any two of
// its points. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_set)
interface IConvexShape
{ }

// Marks a shape that is locally flat everywhere: every point has a neighborhood
// like a line (for 1D shapes) or a disk (for 2D shapes). Excludes T-junctions
// and self-intersections. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IManifold)
interface IManifold
{ }

// Marks a shape that admits a consistent global orientation (a two-sided
// surface; the Moebius strip is the standard counterexample).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orientability)
interface IOrientable
{ }

// Marks a shape consisting of a single connected piece.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connected_space)
interface IConnected
{ }

//==
// # IFitted-shape interface
//
// What every fit result has in common: the residual statistics of the fit.
// The shape itself is deliberately not part of the interface — each fit names
// its own shape field (Line, Plane, Circle, Sphere), and a caller that wants
// the shape already knows which fit it is holding. What a caller does NOT want
// to write per shape is the tolerance check, which is what this interface makes
// writable once. The implementing types are in `geometry.types.plato`.

// Reports how well a fitted shape matches the samples it was fitted to.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodness_of_fit)
interface IFitted
{
    Quality(x: Self): FitQuality;
}

//==
// # IGeometry bounds, point sets, measures, and centroids
//
// What a geometric entity reports about its own extent: an axis-aligned bounding
// region, the finite ordered set of defining points, the length / area / volume
// measures, and the centre of mass under uniform density. All measures are
// unit-agnostic Numbers in coordinate units; physical units are assigned by the
// application, not the geometry.

//==
// # Bounds

// Has a finite axis-aligned bounding rectangle enclosing every point of the shape.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_bounding_box)
interface IBounded2D
{
    Bounds(x: Self): Bounds2D;
}

// Has a finite axis-aligned bounding box enclosing every point of the shape.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounding_volume)
interface IBounded3D
{
    Bounds(x: Self): Bounds3D;
}

//==
// # Point sets

// Exposes the finite ordered set of defining points of a 2D entity: the vertices
// of a polygon, the endpoints of a segment, the samples of a scatter.
interface IPointSet2D
    inherits IGeometry2D
{
    Points(x: Self): Array<Point2D>;
}

// Exposes the finite ordered set of defining points of a 3D entity.
interface IPointSet3D
    inherits IGeometry3D
{
    Points(x: Self): Array<Point3D>;
}

//==
// # Measures
//
// Unit-agnostic measures: lengths in coordinate units, areas in squared units,
// volumes in cubed units.

// Has a finite total length: segments, polylines, and bounded curve spans.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arc_length)
interface ILength
{
    Length(x: Self): Number;
}
